summary: try/catch lets your program handle an error and keep running. throw reports an error from your own code when a value breaks the rules.
notes: catch (error) catches every kind of error. error.name says which kind (Error, RangeError) and error.message gives the reason.
To handle only one kind, check error instanceof RangeError inside catch and throw the others again.
finally runs every time, whether or not an error was thrown.
pitfall: Writing throw "bad score" with a plain string works, but error.message is then undefined. Throw new Error("bad score") so the message is saved.
contrast: JavaScript uses try/catch/finally like Java, but catch takes no error type and catches everything, and no compiler makes you handle errors. Some mistakes are not errors at all: Number("abc") is NaN and 170 / 0 is Infinity.
